item.title: Federal judge blocks FCC from reviewing ABC station licenses early as part of agency's spat with network
item.description: A federal judge ordered the Federal Communications Commission to halt its review of eight ABC station licenses in a win for the Disney-owned network.
item.content:encoded:
A federal judge ordered Wednesday that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) halt its early review of broadcasting licenses of eight ABC stations as part of the agency's intense feud with the Disney-owned network.

U.S. District Judge Loren L. AliKhan ruled in favor of ABC, who sued the FCC on First Amendment grounds after the agency announced it was moving up the license renewals of eight stations owned by the network years ahead of schedule. 

"This is not a close case," AliKhan wrote in the ruling. 

"Today’s decision is an important victory for the First Amendment. We thank the court for its careful consideration," an ABC News spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

DISNEY SUES FCC OVER ‘RETALIATORY CAMPAIGN AGAINST ABC,’ SEEKS TO BLOCK EARLY RENEWAL PROCEEDINGS

"While we appreciate the district court denying in part Disney’s request for preliminary injunctive relief, the portion of the decision granting Disney’s motion is wrong on the facts and wrong on the law—as controlling Supreme Court precedent makes clear," an FCC spokesperson said in a statement. "The FCC looks forward to prevailing in full on this matter. We will continue to use our lawful authority to hold broadcasters accountable to their public interest obligations."

FCC Chairman Brendan Carr has called for early renewal of eight ABC-owned stations' licenses in April. The licenses were originally scheduled to be renewed between 2028 and 2031.

KFSN-TV in Fresno, KABC-TV in Los Angeles, KGO-TV in San Francisco, WLS-TV in Chicago, WABC-TV in New York, WTVD in North Carolina, WPVI-TV in Philadelphia and KTRK-TV in Houston were the stations named by the FCC. 

FCC BOSS BRENDAN CARR MAINTAINS EARLY ABC LICENSE RENEWAL IS ABOUT DEI PROBE, NOT JIMMY KIMMEL CONTROVERSY

While the FCC maintained the license crackdown was focused on the legality of Disney’s diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) practices, Carr's announcement came as tensions reignited between President Donald Trump and ABC late-night host Jimmy Kimmel.

Kimmel had quipped First Lady Melania Trump had the glow of an "expectant widow" on his show, a joke made days before a gunman targeted members of the Trump administration at the White House Correspondents' Association Dinner but caught national attention after the assassination attempt. Both the First Lady and President Trump called for ABC to take action against Kimmel at the time.

Carr had previously leveled a thinly-veiled threat against Disney last year over controversial remarks Kimmel made about the assassination of Turning Point USA founder Charlie Kirk.

'THE VIEW' EASED UP ON POLITICAL CANDIDATE BOOKINGS AMID FCC INQUIRY, REPORT SAYS

The FCC separately launched a probe into ABC's daytime talk show "The View" in an effort to upend its status as a bona fide news program, which exempts the network from abiding by longstanding rules requiring equal time for political candidates.

In previous court filings, ABC has claimed that the actions taken by the FCC has had a chilling effect on the network's free speech, pointing to how "The View" has refrained from inviting political candidates onto the show as a result of the crackdown.

item.title: U2 pays tribute to Dolly Parton during NFL Thanksgiving Eve halftime show
item.description: Ahead of the Jay-Z Super Bowl LVI halftime show, U2's Thanksgiving Eve set at SoFi Stadium honored Dolly Parton with "Torn," her final recording.
item.content:encoded:
If the impending Jay-Z Super Bowl LXI halftime show isn’t your cup of tea, might I interest you in some U2 on the day before Thanksgiving?

U2 started their Thanksgiving Eve halftime performance playing the hits. But things took a weepy turn when the lights were lowered at SoFi Stadium. Appearing on a screen surrounding the stage in the middle of the field was Dolly Parton.

"Co-written by U2, Dolly and Johnny McDaid, ‘Torn’ is a tender country song detailing broken family ties that holds wider resonances," Parton’s official website says. "Parton recorded the song in Nashville, Tennessee in June this year, making it her final recorded vocal performance prior to her passing on August 25, 2026. ‘Torn’ is produced by Jacknife Lee and also features Daniel Lanois playing pedal steel."

item.title: Packers' Christian Watson takes massive hit from Rams' Kamren Kinchens, leads to defender's ejection
item.description: Christian Watson was briefly knocked out on a helmet hit from Kamren Kinchens, who was disqualified, as the Packers receiver is evaluated for a concussion.
item.content:encoded:
Green Bay Packers wide receiver Christian Watson took a huge hit from Los Angeles Rams defensive back Kamren Kinchens during the second quarter their game on Wednesday night.

Packers quarterback Jordan Love lofted a pass toward the sideline in Watson’s direction. Kinchens came in and lowered the boom. Kinchens connected with Watson’s helmet on the play.

The Green Bay receiver was briefly knocked out as trainers came over and checked him out. He was able to walk to the locker room under his own power.

Kinchens was disqualified from the game.

Watson had been playing well before the injury. He had four catches for 65 yards and a touchdown. Packers kicker Trey Smack ended the drive with a field goal to tie the game at 13.

The Packers said Watson was being evaluated for a concussion and was questionable to return to the game. He was later ruled out.

Kinchens had two pass breakups before being thrown out of the game.

Green Bay and Los Angeles entered the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve game in the thick of the playoff race. Both teams were 6-4 and fighting to stay afloat in their respective divisional races.

The Packers were in last place in the NFC North Division – two games behind the Detroit Lions and Chicago Bears in the loss column. The Rams were technically behind the Seattle Seahawks in the NFC West. Both teams are trailing the San Francisco 49ers.

item.title: FedEx cargo jet overshoots runway at Miami International Airport and stops just short of busy road
item.description: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop at Miami International Airport after a FedEx cargo jet overran the runway, causing Thanksgiving flight delays.
item.content:encoded:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a ground stop at Miami International Airport Wednesday evening due to a disabled FedEx aircraft after it overshot the runway, disrupting flights amid the busy Thanksgiving holiday travel rush.

Video from the scene shows a large FedEx cargo jet sitting near a fence that runs next to a busy road. The airport confirmed the aircraft overran Runway 26R, prompting all runways to close except for Runway 9R. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the airport and reported no injuries.

The incident comes nearly three months after a Prime Air cargo jet overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport, killing five people.

FAA ISSUES GROUND DELAY AT CHICAGO O'HARE DUE TO 'EQUIPMENT OUTAGE'

In a statement provided to Fox News Digital shortly before 10 p.m., the FAA said flights would be "resuming shortly" at the airport.

The FAA said FedEx Flight 910, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 arriving from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis, Tennessee, ran off the runway after landing in Miami.

No injuries have been reported, according to the agency.

The FAA is investigating the incident.

FedEx confirmed the incident in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying the plane's crew was safe.

"FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport," a spokesperson said. "We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries."

FedEx added that it was coordinating with investigators.

According to an advisory issued by the FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center, the ground stop took effect at 8:16 p.m.

In its advisory, the FAA said a disabled aircraft caused the ground stop and indicated a medium probability that the restrictions could be extended.

The FAA said the pause was scheduled to remain in place until 9:45 p.m.

WORST AIRPORTS FOR THANKSGIVING TRAVEL CHAOS RANKED AS MAJOR US HUBS TOP LIST

According to an updated FAA advisory, Miami International Airport was experiencing average delays of 47 minutes, with maximum delays reaching two hours on Wednesday evening.

The airport encouraged passengers to check directly with their airlines for flight updates before heading to the airport.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Miami International Airport and the FAA for comment.

This is a developing story, check back for updates.

item.title: USC suspends entire marching band from UCLA game over crude sign prank on Bruins campus
item.description: The USC Trojan Marching Band is barred from the Rose Bowl rivalry game after students allegedly vandalized UCLA's Wasserman Football Center sign overnight.
item.content:encoded:
USC pulled its marching band from Saturday's rivalry game at the Rose Bowl following a late-night campus prank at UCLA.

Ahead of the Big Ten matchup between No. 15 USC and No. 9 UCLA, officials barred the Trojan Marching Band from its pregame and halftime shows after members allegedly vandalized signage at the Wasserman Football Center.

The incident capped off a spirited Tuesday night in Los Angeles.

An hour after the latest College Football Playoff rankings dropped, USC held its annual Conquest pep rally featuring a mock fight between the USC and UCLA mascots. The marching band performed and several USC players attended. Head coach Lincoln Riley did not make an appearance.

ARMY CADETS SNEAK INTO NAVY'S STADIUM TO LEAVE A SPECIAL MESSAGE IN THE UPPER DECK

Later that night, according to UCLA's Daily Bruin, band members allegedly crossed town and removed letters from the Wasserman Football Center's exterior sign to spell "ass Football Center."

The vandalism left the facility temporarily branded as the "ASS Football Center." USC President Beong-Soo Kim responded Wednesday with a formal apology to UCLA.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL CORPORATE OVERLORDS RUIN ANOTHER CLASSIC RIVALRY GAME WITH STUPID NEW NAME

"This morning, we learned that a portion of UCLA's campus had been vandalized by individual students belonging to the Trojan Marching Band. This conduct runs contrary to USC's values and is unacceptable," Kim wrote in a statement to the Trojan community.

"We are cooperating fully with law enforcement and an investigation is underway. Appropriate interim actions will be or have already been taken, and any student ultimately found responsible will be subject to discipline under university policy."

The move will sideline hundreds of student musicians for the actions of a few. Kim added that the decision was made jointly with band leadership.

"We want to express our deepest apologies to the entire UCLA community. Our rivalry is one of the great traditions in college athletics, and it has always rested on mutual respect. What happened on UCLA's campus last night has no place in this tradition," Kim wrote.

"Out of respect for UCLA, and to provide time to reflect on the collective responsibility we share to uphold our university's values, the university and Trojan Marching Band's leadership have decided that the band will not take the field for their traditional pre-game and halftime performances at the Rose Bowl this Saturday."

A USC spokesperson declined to share details on the damages or disciplinary process, telling Fox News Digital.

"The university does not have further comment as the investigation into the matter is ongoing."

UCLA offered Fox News Digital a much looser response: "Go Bruins. Beat SC!"

The Crosstown Showdown has a long history of rivalry week pranks and campus raids. Every November, USC students wrap the Tommy Trojan statue in duct tape to protect it from blue and gold paint, while UCLA students pull overnight shifts guarding the Bruin Bear statue and hiding it under a wooden box.

item.title: Super Bowl champion, Steelers teammate of Aaron Rodgers shows support for quarterback after dramatic fallout
item.description: Marquez Valdes-Scantling showed support for Aaron Rodgers after the four-time MVP was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers following his remarks about Mike McCarthy.
item.content:encoded:
Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling expressed his appreciation for Aaron Rodgers amid his fallout with head coach Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers was released by the Steelers shortly after he went scorched earth on his 62-year-old coach on Wednesday. Valdes-Scantling, who spent four seasons with Rodgers when they were both members of the Green Bay Packers, showed support for his former quarterback.

"It's one of those things you never want to see," Valdes-Scantling told reporters. "Me and Aaron have a great relationship. He's become one of my closest friends that I've made in this league. I wouldn't be where I am today without him. He's opened up so many doors for me and taught me so many things about football. Seeing that is something you never want to see because I think he's the greatest player to ever play this game at that position."

The two-time Super Bowl champion is currently on the Steelers' practice squad after being released by the Los Angeles Chargers earlier this season. While he hasn't appeared in any regular-season games this season with the Steelers, he did appear in five games with Pittsburgh last season.

The Steelers announced they were benching Rodgers and making him inactive on Tuesday night, and on Wednesday the four-time MVP appeared on ESPN's "The Pat McAfee Show" and held nothing back on McCarthy.

The Steelers officially released Rodgers shortly after the interview.

item.title: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart' after judges question key charges
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared his corruption trial "fell apart" as judges urged prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases.
item.content:encoded:
The decade-long legal battle against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suffered a major blow Wednesday after judges cast doubt on key corruption charges, prompting the Israeli leader to declare that his trial had "fallen apart" and demand an immediate end to the proceedings.

A three-judge panel at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara consider dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu, questioned whether a criminal offense occurred in a second case and recommended resolving a third through a plea deal.

"Today, the trial fell apart," Netanyahu said in an evening address following the proceedings, according to The Times of Israel.

FROM INTELLIGENCE SHARING TO MISSILE DEFENSE, HOW ISRAEL'S PARTNERSHIP PROTECTS AMERICAN SECURITY

"Ten years ago, I said, ‘There will be nothing because there was nothing.’ But it took 10 years for this truth to be revealed to everyone," he said.

"Citizens of Israel, this trial must end immediately. And what also needs to end immediately is what came out of it — the hatred, the incitement, the division."

The court's intervention dealt a major setback to prosecutors more than six years after Netanyahu's trial began and roughly a decade after authorities launched the initial probe into him.

Judges had summoned Baharav-Miara to court Wednesday amid concerns over the strength of the prosecution's evidence and whether continuing the cases served the public interest.

"We’re now at a crossroad and need to rechart a new path," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told the attorney general, according to The New York Sun.

"Public interest dictates a need to rethink."

NETANYAHU REVEALS HE WANTS AMERICAN FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL TO 'DRAW DOWN TO ZERO'

She and her colleagues, Judges Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham, stressed that their comments were preliminary, did not constitute a verdict and applied only to Netanyahu because they still had to hear the other defendants’ testimony, The Jerusalem Post reported.

Baharav-Miara signaled that prosecutors would review the judges' recommendations and weigh their options.

Netanyahu faces charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust stemming from three corruption investigations.

Prosecutors announced the charges in November 2019 and formally filed the indictment in January 2020, and Netanyahu consistently denied wrongdoing.

The most serious charge, Case 4000, centers on allegations that Netanyahu granted regulatory favors to Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on the Walla news website, which was then controlled by businessman Shaul Elovitch.

Judges questioned whether prosecutors presented sufficient evidence to secure a conviction. In Case 2000, prosecutors also allege Netanyahu negotiated for favorable coverage from Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper publisher Arnon Mozes in exchange for legislation to weaken rival newspaper Israel Hayom.

TRUMP WANTS LARGEST-EVER ISRAELI HEAVY BOMB TRANSFER — BUT PROPOSAL HAS CONGRESS PREPARING FOR $2.8B FIGHT

The proposed deal never materialized, and judges questioned whether a criminal offense had happened.

Case 1000 centers on allegations that Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, received almost $300,000 in gifts from Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan and Australian billionaire James Packer.

Judges suggested resolving that case through an agreement. Zion Amir, an attorney who previously represented Netanyahu in the proceedings, rejected the prospect of a settlement.

In his address Wednesday, Netanyahu also accused investigators of pressuring his political associates to testify against him and described the toll the investigations had taken on his family. 

"Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my wife and my sons," he said.

"Of delusional interrogations. Of character assassination. Of grave incitement that wounds the soul. Who will give us back those 10 years?"

Netanyahu, who requested a presidential pardon in November 2025 without admitting guilt, also called on his political opponents to set aside their differences and form a unity government.

"The boycotts must end, and now," Netanyahu said.

"I know what enormous and immediate dangers the State of Israel faces. There is only one way to deal with them. To unite in order to deal with them. We must unite to secure the future of Israel — no less than that, and immediately."

item.title: Aaron Rodgers' ex-Packers teammate makes bold prediction about QB’s NFL future after shocking Steelers exit
item.description: Aaron Rodgers was released by the Pittsburgh Steelers after claiming on "The Pat McAfee Show" that coach Mike McCarthy slept through team meetings.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers’ time with the Pittsburgh Steelers ended abruptly just one day before Thanksgiving. The team cut ties with the veteran quarterback shortly after benching him and following his disparaging comments about coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday.

Rodgers, who was in his second season with the Steelers, alleged that McCarthy had been sleeping through team meetings.

"That ship has sailed," Rodgers said about his stint in Pittsburgh. While his future in the NFL remains unclear, but former longtime Green Bay Packers teammate Clay Matthews offered a bold prediction.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"I think this is the last time we see him in the league. I don't think another team wants him as their quarterback." Matthews said on Netflix ahead of the Los Angeles Rams and Green Bay Packers kicked off for the NFL's first-ever Thanksgiving Eve game.

The Packers drafted Matthews in the first round in 2009. Matthews went on to spend a decade with Rodgers, helping Green Bay win Super Bowl XLV during his second season.

WHAT’S YOUR TAKE: WILL AARON RODGERS PLAY ANOTHER SNAP THIS SEASON?

"It's sad, (Rodgers is) one of the greatest quarterbacks we've ever had in this National Football League. For him to end his career like this, walking off the football field like this, that's very sad," Pro Football Hall of Famer Michael Irvin added.

The NFL's trade deadline for this season had already passed by the time Rodgers was released, meaning the four-time league MVP will have to go through waivers before another potentially interested team claims him. If Rodgers makes it through waivers unclaimed, he would then be an unrestricted free agent.

Mason Rudolph is expected to start when the Black Friday game against the Denver Broncos kicks off. Rodgers suggested he was unaware he wouldn't be the starter going forward until a teammate alerted him.

AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS

Rodgers said Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth said during a phone call, "I can't believe they're doing this."

Rodgers said he asked, "'Doing what?'"

Although his ending wasn't ideal, Rodgers expressed appreciation for his time with the Steelers.

"I thanked Mike T [Tomlin] last year for giving me that joy and passion back. I mean, in the two years I've been here, I've made some super tight friendships, and we got such a good group of guys, such a great veteran leadership, guys that give a s---, guys that play hard, great personalities all over the board," he said.

item.title: TNA's KC Navarro details battle to get to Destination X pay-per-view in midst of travel nightmare
item.description: TNA wrestler KC Navarro reveals how he and Tasha Steelz nearly missed Destination X amid flight chaos, sprinting to catch a 20-minute connection in time.
item.content:encoded:
Total Nonstop Action Wrestling (TNA) successfully put on a thrilling Destination X pay-per-view earlier this month despite a ground stop that hampered travel for millions in North America.

Several TNA wrestlers were affected by the flight issues. Many made it work, while others were forced to skip the show. Still, the show went on. KC Navarro ended up winning the men’s Ultimate X match and earning a shot at the X Division Championship.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

But Navarro wasn’t exempt from the chaos.

"Me and Tasha Steelz were actually on the same flight," he explained to OutKick Dropkick. "Funny enough, the two winners of the Ultimate X were on the same flight, almost didn't have winners. But we were traveling together and we had about a one-hour delay and we were there early. We were supposed to have the first flight out. We didn't fly out ‘til like an hour or two after. It was a bit of a delay. I remember we landed for our connection and almost missed our connection. And it was like a 20-minute connection like we had to get to. We got there within 10 minutes ‘cause we ran, hard. We ran like it was like a marathon. I don't know how we made it, but we ended up making our gate because we wanted to be there."

Navarro said he felt bad for those who were unable to make the show because everyone involved in the pay-per-view was trying hard to get there. Fabian Aichner, who was in the Ultimate X match as well, drove "like 10 hours," according to Navarro, to get to Edmonton, Alberta, Canada.

"That's the type of team we have, man, and I've been asked this question a lot of like,, ‘Was everybody nervous and that was it, was it like everybody anxious?’ To be completely honest, I think we were all motivated. Obviously, I think if there was any anxiousness, it was ‘cause we were worried about everybody's safety. But we knew our backs were against the wall, and I personally feel with the cards that we were dealt, man, we put on a hell of a pay-per-view, and I would say it's definitely top three of this year of what we did this year, and I'm so proud of my team and I'm so blessed to be a part of the TNA wrestling team."

Navarro said TNA wrestlers and personnel being able to put on a show in a dire situation showed the resilience of the company and the people who work there.

A true "underdog" story.

"It's kind of like my story, right? They're always gonna be the underdog. Everybody always counts out TNA. But how many times has TNA survived and I feel like they always do whatever they can to get back to their fans, man," he told OutKick Dropkick. "Like, there was no canceling that show, and it's because the roster wanted to be there.

"We wanted to put on a show. We didn't want to be like, ‘Oh, there's a ground stoppage up, we can't make it,’ none of us. We didn't care if we all had to drive there. We were going to get to Edmonton, and we all did, man, and we put on a great pay-per-view, and it just shows the resilience of our locker room and the entire team as a whole."

Navarro will go for gold on Dec. 18 against Amazing Red in El Paso, Texas.

item.title: Six Florida family members killed in plane crash on way home from fishing trip identified
item.description: The Cessna 210 was descending 10,000 feet per minute when it crashed 2 miles off Horn Island, Mississippi, after a Louisiana fishing trip, the FAA said.
item.content:encoded:
Six family members from Florida were killed Tuesday when the small plane they were aboard crashed off the Mississippi coast on their way home from a fishing trip, according to reports.

Those killed were identified by Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. as Brent Stokes, 50; Hunter Stokes, 16; Michael Knox, 43; Arlyn Knox, 43; Charles Holden Knox, 12; and Truett Knox, 10.

The family, from Fort Myers, had been on a fishing trip in Louisiana, Lynd said. Brent Stokes was piloting the Cessna 210 aircraft, which was descending at 10,000 feet per minute when it crashed, the Federal Aviation Administration said.

4 FLORIDA FAMILY MEMBERS FOUND DEAD AFTER SMALL PLANE GOES DOWN OFF THE BAHAMAS

Brent Stokes was traveling with his son, Hunter Stokes, and his sister, Arlyn Knox, NOLA.com reported. Arlyn and Michael Knox were the parents of Charles Holden Knox and Truett Knox.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Lynd's office for comment.

COAST GUARD SUSPENDS SEARCH FOR BOSTON-BOUND MEDEVAC PLANE OFF NANTUCKET WITH 6 ON BOARD

The plane lost contact with air traffic control at about 3:45 p.m., according to authorities.

The downed aircraft was found 2 miles off Horn Island, Mississippi. Divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources located the remains of all six people inside the fuselage after an hours-long search, the U.S. Coast Guard said.

HELICOPTER CRASH NEAR MIAMI LEAVES AT LEAST 1 DEAD, 2 INJURED: REPORT

"This is a heartbreaking outcome, and our deepest sympathies are with the families and loved ones who are facing an unimaginable loss," said Cmdr. Trevor Blount, the Coast Guard Sector Mobile search and rescue mission coordinator. 

"While this is not the outcome any of us had hoped for, we are grateful for the strong interagency coordination that enabled us to swiftly locate those aboard the aircraft and provide closure to their families."

Paradise Outfitters, which offers sport fishing charters in Venice, Louisiana, said it had gotten to know the Stokes and Knox families over the years.

GOT A TIP?

"Even after Brent built a boat like ours, he still wanted our captains out there with him, we continued to show him and his family the waters we all love. Those days together meant so much to our crew," the company said Wednesday in a Facebook post. 

"Please pray for the Stokes and Knox families and all who love them as they face the days ahead. Please keep our captains and our Venice fishing community in your prayers, too, as we grieve the loss of our dear friends."

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the crash.

item.title: Taking Ozempic or Wegovy could lead to extra cancer screenings, new study suggests
item.description: A study for the Radiological Society of North America links GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy to higher breast density on mammograms in 62.5% of women.
item.content:encoded:
Women taking popular weight loss medications may have higher breast density on mammograms and require more follow-up imaging, even when none of those abnormalities turn out to be cancer.

That's according to a new study scheduled for presentation at the annual meeting of the Radiological Society of North America, Nov. 29-Dec. 3, 2026, in Chicago.

The study examined 107 women, ages 34 to 79, who took GLP-1 receptor agonists, a class of drugs that includes Ozempic and Wegovy, for weight loss for at least one year.

POPULAR WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS MAY PLAY SURPRISING ROLE IN CANCER OUTCOMES

Participants lost between six and 107 pounds, with an average loss of 40 pounds. Researchers reviewed 214 screening mammograms taken before and after at least a year of treatment, according to the study.

Specialized software showed that breast density rose by at least one category in 62.5% of participants who took GLP-1s. Eight women moved up two density categories.

Radiologists also saw smaller breasts in roughly 58% to 79% of patients, depending on the reviewer, and increased skin thickening in about 9% to 18%.

Higher breast density is generally tied to a greater risk of breast cancer and can make tumors harder to spot on X-rays.

However, the pattern seen after weight loss likely reflects a shift in proportions rather than more dense tissue growing, according to lead author Dr. Eva C. Gombos, a diagnostic radiologist at Brigham and Women's Hospital in Boston.

POPULAR WEIGHT LOSS DRUGS MAY HELP PROTECT AGAINST A DEADLY DISEASE, DOCTOR SAYS

"It was surprising that 62.5% of women had increased BI-RADS breast density despite substantial weight loss, with no decreases observed," Gombos said in a release.

"This may reflect disproportionate loss of breast fat, causing a relative increase in mammographic density even as absolute fibroglandular volume decreases."

When a person loses significant fat from the breast, the remaining milk ducts and supportive tissue — known as fibroglandular tissue — can make up a larger share of what shows up on the image, even if the total amount of that tissue did not grow.

Gombos also noted that losing breast fat and volume can leave extra skin or skin folds, which may help explain why skin and connective tissue strands looked more prominent on some scans.

Nearly 22.4% of the women were called back for additional imaging after screening, compared with an average U.S. recall rate of about 10%.

Two women had technical recalls to repeat scans due to positioning or imaging issues. Four women were referred for biopsies, and all four came back benign. All other callbacks also turned out to be benign or negative, including three simple cysts.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

Gombos emphasized that the findings should not pose a concern for women taking GLP-1 drugs or cause them to skip routine screenings.

Whether these density shifts carry any long-term change in breast cancer risk remains unclear and needs more research.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

The study was retrospective and looked back at medical records rather than following patients forward in a controlled trial, the researchers noted.

It did not establish whether the imaging changes affect long-term breast cancer risk.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

Gombos recommends that women tell their breast imaging team if they use GLP-1 medications or have recently lost a significant amount of weight because it helps technologists and radiologists more accurately compare new scans to older ones.

Novo Nordisk, maker of Ozempic and Wegovy, emphasized that it continuously monitors the safety profile of its medicines, reviewing emerging data as it becomes available.

"Individuals respond to treatment uniquely based on multiple biological and lifestyle factors, which means outcomes can vary from person to person," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

"We recommend that all patients maintain close contact with their healthcare professional to discuss any questions or concerns about their treatment, and for ongoing guidance and careful monitoring."

item.title: 2nd Circuit deals blow to Manhattan DA, breathes new life into Trump's hush money appeal
item.description: President Donald Trump's bid to move his New York hush money case to federal court is revived after the 2nd Circuit cited errors in a prior denial.
item.content:encoded:
A federal appeals court handed President Donald Trump a legal victory Monday, reviving his bid to wrest his New York hush money case from state court and potentially overturn his felony conviction on presidential immunity grounds.

The 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals ruled that an August decision by the late U. S. District Judge Alvin Hellerstein, a Clinton appointee who died in October, that denied Trump's second transfer bid was improper.

The criminal case centered on Trump's reimbursement of his then-attorney Michael Cohen, who paid adult film actress Stormy Daniels $130,000 shortly before the 2016 election to keep her from publicizing an alleged sexual encounter with Trump a decade earlier. 

Trump, who denies the encounter, was found guilty in May 2024 of 34 felony counts of falsifying business records.

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT REFUSES TO REHEAR TRUMP APPEAL OF $83M E JEAN CARROLL DEFAMATION JUDGMENT

At his January 2025 sentencing — days before his second inauguration — Trump received an unconditional discharge, leaving him with no prison time or fine, though the felony conviction remains on his record.

Trump has continued fighting to move the case out of state court, scoring a victory before a three-judge appellate panel Monday.

"We disagree with the district court," said circuit judges Raymond J. Lohier Jr., an Obama appointee; José A. Cabranes, a Clinton appointee; and John M. Walker Jr., a George H. W. Bush appointee.

The panel found Hellerstein made two legal errors: A federal official can still seek removal after being convicted, and Trump showed "good cause" to file a second removal notice. A full written opinion will follow "in due course," the judges wrote.

Trump's attorneys argued in a September brief that the legal landscape had fundamentally changed since his first attempt to transfer the case in 2023. They pointed to the Supreme Court's July 2024 immunity decision, arguing that Manhattan prosecutors had relied on evidence of Trump's presidential activities at trial that the high court subsequently deemed off-limits.

Trump attorney Robert Giuffra Jr. warned that leaving the case in New York's judicial system could significantly delay the president's ability to seek relief from the nation's highest court, arguing Trump "will likely have to wait years."

TRUMP'S LAWYERS PUT DEM AG ON NOTICE FOR TARGETING HIS FAMILY IN NY FRAUD FIGHT: 'CANNOT STAND'

Manhattan prosecutors had urged the 2nd Circuit to uphold Hellerstein's denial, arguing Trump engaged in "strategic delay" by testing his immunity claim in state court first and seeking a transfer only when he believed he would lose. They also maintained that falsifying business records over a personal payoff had nothing to do with official duties.

The ruling puts the question of federal jurisdiction before U.S. District Judge Lewis J. Liman, who inherited the case after Hellerstein's death. The appellate panel also requested that New York courts suspend further proceedings while the jurisdiction dispute is resolved.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

If Liman grants the transfer, the federal court will adopt the conviction, setting up a clash over whether it must be vacated under the Supreme Court's immunity standard. Moving the case would not allow Trump to pardon himself, however, because the underlying charges remain New York state offenses outside the reach of a presidential pardon.

Fox News Digital reached out to the Manhattan District Attorney's Office and Trump's legal team for comment but did not receive a response by publication time.

item.title: Ms Rachel calls silence on Gaza conflict 'f---ed up,' says it's upset her so much she now swears

Tony Romo, 46, has officially resurfaced; unfortunately for him, it's nowhere close to an NFL broadcast booth.

On Wednesday, sports gaming company Betr announced that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback is joining the brand as its first-ever Chief Predictions Officer.

Early details on the sponsorship note that Romo will create content, deliver sports picks, and push Betr’s gaming products alongside a roster that includes Johnny Manziel and Patrick Beverley (not the most esteemed troika of sports personalities).

Romo's full statement on the partnership read:

"I've spent my entire career trying to anticipate what's going to happen next, whether that was on the field or in the broadcast booth.

"Now I get to put those instincts to work in a completely new way with Betr. What Jake, Joey and the team are building is really interesting because they're bringing so many different ways for fans to engage with sports and gaming together in one place.

"I'm looking forward to having some fun, making predictions and being part of where this company is headed. And I've got a pretty good feeling about what's coming next."

Betr posted on X, quoting Romo's announcement post: "Got our guy. Pumped to have you on the team."

It marks Romo’s first public gig since parting ways with CBS Sports on Oct. 2, abruptly ending his nine-year run as the network's lead NFL analyst.

On Sept. 1, Romo pleaded no contest, losing his driving privileges for six months and entering an alcohol assessment program. Romo attributed the incident to an over-reliance on alcohol stemming from football-related injuries.

item.title: Steelers officially release Aaron Rodgers and keep coach Mike McCarthy on the job despite embarrassing claims
item.description: Mike McCarthy keeps his Steelers job despite an ice cream assistant leak and Aaron Rodgers' claims he snores in meetings, saying "I know how to win."
item.content:encoded:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are sticking with Mike McCarthy, but the embarrassment the coach must endure to stay at his post has not stopped since Aaron Rodgers pulled back the curtain on his failings – because other players have leaked unflattering details about the coach.

The most bizarre leak is that Mike McCarthy has an ice cream sandwich assistant.

You read correctly.

AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY DISAGREEMENTS AT HEART OF QUARTERBACK'S BENCHING BY THE STEELERS

Former NFL veteran Breiden Fehoko, who played three years in the NFL and at LSU in college, posted on X that a Steelers player texted him McCarthy has a personal assistant who brings him ice cream sandwiches on demand.

And that is true according to a source who confirmed it for OutKick and Fox News Digital. The coach has been seen getting ice cream brought to him and often greets the delivery with obvious satisfaction.

'WHAT THE F--K, CALL IT!': AARON RODGERS AND MIKE MCCARTHY CURSE AT EACH OTHER DURING HOT MIC MOMENT

Despite that and other unbecoming claims Rodgers made about McCarthy on the "Pat McAfee Show" on Wednesday, including that he falls asleep and snores during meetings, misses meetings and is generally "unwell," the Steelers are not firing McCarthy.

They did, in fact, make official the release of Rodgers on Wednesday, which they didn't plan to do before his McAfee interview. But the club is privately confirming an ESPN report that McCarthy remains in his post and has the organization's full support.

That was obvious once the Steelers made McCarthy available to reporters for a previously not scheduled news conference, a move that would not happen if he was being dismissed.

In that press conference, McCarthy made a case for himself remaining as the coach.

"I know how to win," McCarthy said. "And that's the facts. This is my third program. And I plan on winning here because of the men, because of this organization. We've got started and the opportunity we have to learn and grow today because of some of the things that, frankly, should have been talked about earlier.

"So, this is a growth opportunity that I intend to take full advantage of it."

McCarthy said he met with his player leadership council on Wednesday and came away convinced he remains the right person to lead the team as coach.

"Yes, I do," McCarthy said. "And I will say that I just came from a, you know, player council meeting. I thought that it was a meeting, very direct, very honest. I appreciated the opportunity to talk through numerous, numerous things that have been underlined, comments that were brought to discussion to, you know, to the forefront.

"So I'm proud of our leadership. I'll say that. And more importantly, I love the urgency that everybody had coming out of that meeting."

McCarthy did not give a clear explanation why he decided to bench Rodgers in the first place, a move that led to all this drama. All McCarthy said was that Rodgers went outside the bounds of his job and that got him benched.

"There was an ultimatum made, clearly outside of his job description, so it was my decision to bench him," McCarthy said without adding detail.

Despite this, the Steelers' player told OutKick and Fox News Digital he thinks Rodgers is more respected among his former teammates than McCarthy. But, he added, he understands why the decision to cut Rodgers was made.

Publicly, players are paying Rodgers their respects.

"This is something you never want to see," said receiver Marquez Valdes-Scantling. "Obviously, we have a great relationship. He's one of my closest friends that I've made in this league. I wouldn't be where I am today without him."

McCarthy was not asked about his ice-cream-fetcher. He was asked about claims Rodgers made. McCarthy admitted to some but refuted others.

The coach confirmed that he accidentally broke down the Steelers' locker room with "1-2-3 Packers" at halftime against Philadelphia, calling it an "embarrassing moment."

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

But McCarthy pushed back against Rodgers's claims that he fell asleep in meetings and missed walk-throughs, saying he took issue with how his commitment to the job was characterized.

McCarthy also said it is not accurate that he holds a grudge against Rodgers for getting fired by the Packers in 2018.

The problem McCarthy faces in all this is that Rodgers apparently has more credibility among players than he does – at least privately. And the only way he can reclaim that credibility is if the team rallies, starting with Friday's game against the Denver Broncos.

Five minutes later, you hear the snoring again. And less than five minutes after that, he walks out of the room like nothing happened," Rodgers said.

item.title: Major League Baseball owners sue MLB Players Association ahead of rapidly approaching lockout
item.description: Major League Baseball sued the MLBPA in federal court in a move the league calls defensive, as the CBA expires and a lockout threatens the 2027 season.
item.content:encoded:
Well, if you were hoping for a quick resolution to the disagreements between Major League Baseball and the Players Association, you probably shouldn't.

With the expiration of the Collective Bargaining Agreement happening on Monday night, the league and the 30 team owners are set to lock players out of team facilities, training and contact or communication with team officials, in an effort to secure higher profits.

While negotiations between the two sides are ongoing, there's little hope of a resolution before the coming week, as the two sides have fundamental disagreements over how the financial future of the game should be structured. Players want to preserve the system as is, while increasing revenue sharing from higher income teams to lower income teams.

WITH MAJOR LEAGUE BASEBALL'S LOCKOUT LOOMING, WOULD THE LEAGUE'S PROPOSAL 'FIX' BASEBALL?

Owners want to end baseball's free market and incorporate sports socialism in order to ensure they retain a higher percentage of revenue, pay players less while disguising its motivations with hand-waving virtue signaling to uninformed fans about nonexistent competitive balance issues.

Wednesday, those negotiations became even more contentious.

The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday morning that the league had sued the Players Association in federal court in order to prevent the players from potentially dissolving the union. That tactic could be used by MLBPA to open up the league to antitrust lawsuits, which could jeopardize MLB's unique and very beneficial monopoly position.

While the MLBPA has not threatened to dissolve their status, nor have they officially done so, the league's position is that this was a "defensive" move to retain their bargaining rights.

"Today’s filing is a defensive measure simply intended to keep the parties at the bargaining table to work towards a new collective bargaining agreement and a full 2027 season," said MLB spokesperson Glen Caplin, per MLB.com reporter Mark Feinsand. "We believe the Union is preparing to follow the playbook its new leadership has used against other major professional sports leagues by pretending to ‘disclaim’ its status as the Players’ bargaining representative to pursue an antitrust lawsuit as an end run around the bargaining process.

"Today, we have asked a federal court in the Southern District of New York to proactively disarm the Union’s nuclear option of disclaiming. To be clear, our objective is to protect the collective bargaining process, so that we can remain at the table until we negotiate a new labor agreement."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Well, their obvious objective is to ensure that their antitrust status remains intact, preserving a benefit that likely amounts to billions of dollars in "hidden" value.

The players, predictably, were not pleased.

"The lawsuit filed today by MLB is completely frivolous," they said in a statement. "We will respond appropriately, but MLB's decision to run to court in the middle of negotiations rather than bargain in good faith is incredibly disappointing."

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Owners have not bargained in good faith and do not intend to. Because their position is untenable; it requires a fundamental restructuring of the game in order to increase their share of profits and franchise valuations. Many fans are supportive of this measure, incorrectly believing that there would be improved competitive balance resulting from a salary cap.

There is no competitive balance problem in baseball, for a start, and as the players proposed this week, an increase in revenue sharing or pooled media revenues from teams like the Dodgers and Yankees would accomplish the same goal, giving smaller teams more money for existing, that a salary cap would. But because the cap proposal has nothing to do with competitive balance and everything to do with making owners richer, the league has essentially ignored the players' suggestion.

The league also said that MLBPA "has refused to even consider the cap and floor system during the parties’ negotiations because it hopes to coerce MLB to abandon its position by threatening antitrust litigation." The billionaire owners and Rob Manfred "cannot sit by idly while the Union’s stonewalling and sham tactics jeopardize a full 2027 season," they explained.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

The only party jeopardizing the 2027 season is, of course, ownership. Because they are the ones demanding the game be torn down and redrawn to increase their franchise valuations. The cap proposal would take billions away from players and redistribute it to owners, while doing nothing to impact competitive balance, ticket prices or exorbitant streaming service costs. It's just to make the team owners' assets more valuable while limiting downside and risks.

Hopefully, this is just a negotiating tactic and not a sign of broader issues that could lead to the cancelation of the 2027 season. But with the support of fans who refuse to accept the reality of modern baseball, owners might feel emboldened to do so.

The clock to Opening Day 2027 is already ticking. Fast.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers interview is exactly why ESPN pays Pat McAfee | Bobby Burack
item.description: Aaron Rodgers claims Mike McCarthy is "unwell" and falls asleep in meetings, and the bombshell on "The Pat McAfee Show" is why ESPN pays Pat McAfee.
item.content:encoded:
And that’s why ESPN pays Pat McAfee.

On Wednesday, Aaron Rodgers triggered a release from the Pittsburgh Steelers after delivering a pipe bomb on head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show."

Rodgers referred to McCarthy, who benched him Tuesday night, as "unwell," claiming he frequently falls asleep during team meetings, is disconnected from his players, and takes days to review game film.

He recalled a recent moment in which McCarthy shouted "1-2-3 Packers" during Pittsburgh's 19-16 loss to the Eagles as "the nail in the coffin" of his relationship with his former coach.

"'1-2-3 Packers' is crazy," Rodgers said. "On the bus and in all of our group chats it was talked about, like how was that possible."

HERE IS HOW PAT MCAFEE HAS SURPASSED STEPHEN A SMITH AS THE FACE OF ESPN | BOBBY BURACK

The day was supposed to be quiet until the NFL’s first Thanksgiving Eve broadcast. Instead, McAfee's interview with Rodgers has generated homepage headlines for not just ESPN but also Fox News, CNN, Yahoo, CBS News, and NBC

And for a company that despises crediting other outlets for news in sports, Wednesday's interview emphasized McAfee's value to ESPN.

Nobody else was getting that interview.

Skeptics can debate what any sports commentator is worth. Reports say McAfee’s next deal could be worth $60 million. To ESPN, he's worth a lot.

McAfee's uniquely friendly style of interviews has drawn criticism from the hall monitors of sports media. They've challenged his journalistic integrity, as if they practice it unconditionally. And yet, he has garnered the trust of the biggest names in sports by not displaying the prickly behavior that defines many of his peers.

It works.

READ MORE FROM OUTKICK HERE

His recent guests include Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson, LeBron James, Josh Allen, Brock Lesnar and the commissioners of the NBA, MLB and NHL.

"I'm standing on the truth, that's why it's not emotional for me anymore," Rodgers concluded. "Everyone knows it and everyone talks about it all over the building."

Compare McAfee's reach to ESPN's former biggest star, Stephen A. Smith. At this stage, Smith is relegated to making news by saying racist things about white basketball players. He's an embarrassment.

"This is another example of the power of Pat McAfee," OutKick reporter Jon Root said Wednesday. "He’s able to get a non-PR, insanely honest answer out of Aaron Rodgers, making it the biggest breaking news in the NFL this season."

McAfee can be a headache for ESPN. His dustup with Utah college students was off-putting. But the same rule applies to McAfee as it does to the athletes he interviews.

The more you deliver, the more your bosses accept. His interview with Aaron Rodgers delivered.

It's exactly what ESPN paid for.

item.title: Socialists on blast for pledging to weed money out of politics but accepting business execs' checks anyway
item.description: An investigation of FEC records found 24 corporate executives gave $675,300 to DSA-endorsed candidates like Rashida Tlaib and progressive PACs.
item.content:encoded:
Far-left lawmakers are facing accusations of hypocrisy for criticizing corporate influence in politics while accepting campaign contributions from influential executives in industries including defense and healthcare.

A new investigation looking into Federal Election Commission filings found socialist-aligned candidates who pledged to reject corporate PAC contributions still took the cash from PAC's and corporate executives.

"If you're taking money from them, at least be man enough to admit you're going to take the money," Rep.-elect Jerry Carl, R-Ala., told Fox News Digital in reference to Rep. Rashida Tlaib, D-Mich.

Filings first flagged by anti-DEI nonprofit 1792 Exchange were reviewed by Fox News Digital. They show Tlaib accepted checks in 2023 and 2025 totaling $10,600 from L3Harris executive defense contractor Faisal Munir, even after she authored an op-ed in 2025 criticizing lawmakers who financially benefit from the defense industry.

RADICAL SOCIALIST WING'S HUGE NIGHT REVEALS ASCENDING CLOUT WITHIN DEMOCRATIC PARTY

Other Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) members, such as, Reps.-elect Donavan McKinney, D-Mich., Claire Valdez, D-N.Y., and Darializa Avila Chevalier, D-N.Y., publicly pledged to reject corporate PAC contributions, according to End Citizens United. Yet all three took cash from PACs and corporate executives, as noted in the investigation. 

While still candidates, however, they never specified if their pledge to reject corporate money also applies to the individuals running corporations and those outside PACs. 

On her campaign website, Chevalier calls for banning super PAC money from elections, arguing that the political system "rewards the wealthy elite, corporations, and political machines over working people."

Valdez, similarly, has criticized money in politics and blamed "AIPAC, crypto and AI" for "spending millions and millions of dollars" in "trying to influence the elections."

McKinney denounced the campaign finance system on his website, arguing that it prevents elected officials from addressing voters' concerns.

'SQUAD' RAKES IN RECORD $2.35M WHILE SLAMMING THE DOOR ON COP DONATIONS

Omar Tawakol, CEO of AI advertising platform Rembrand, contributed $13,600 to Tlaib, $7,000 to McKinney and $3,500 each to Valdez and Chevalier.

The initial investigation notes that 24 corporate executives contributed a combined $675,300 to DSA-endorsed congressional candidates during the two previous election cycles. 17 of those 24 contributed $126,300 directly to the DSA-endorsed candidates. 

The other $549,000 went to three progressive political action committees: Justice Democrats, Leaders We Deserve and the Working Families Party PAC, which largely relies on money from corporate executives and other PACs which support the DSA candidates.

Justice Democrats contributed to Chevalier, Tlaib and Valdez, while Leaders We Deserve supported McKinney and Valdez. The Working Families Party PAC supported McKinney.

Justice Democrats received $150,000 from Desmos Studio CEO Eli Luberoff and $85,000 from Hims & Hers Health CEO Andrew Dudum.

Android co-founder Rich Miner contributed $65,000 to Leaders We Deserve, while former Google chief scientist Jeff Dean donated $100,000 to the Working Families Party PAC.

Heritage Foundation chief economist E.J. Antoni spelled out for Fox News Digital how executives often support candidates in hopes of securing regulatory "carve-outs, exemptions, and exclusions" if they are elected to positions where they can introduce or influence related policy in the future. 

The campaign finance records do not establish that any of the executives sought or received preferential treatment in exchange for their contributions.

PROGRESSIVE GROUP'S 182-PAGE BLUEPRINT MAPS OUT POTENTIAL DEM INVESTIGATIONS INTO TRUMP, CORPORATE ALLIES

Keira Havens, founder of Courage for Democracy, the organization behind President Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth impeachment efforts, told Fox News Digital that the "solution" to the "corruption" displayed by the politicians is "accountability." 

DSA-endorsed politicians Valdez, Chevalier, McKinney and Tlaib all did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment, neither did the DSA itself.

The PACs — Justice Democrats, Working Families Party and Leaders We Deserve — also did not respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

item.title: Famed NFL agent reveals potential consequences for Steelers, Mike McCarthy after public Aaron Rodgers rupture
item.description: Famed agent Leigh Steinberg says Aaron Rodgers' public accusations against Steelers coach Mike McCarthy could deter future free agents from Pittsburgh.
item.content:encoded:
Famed NFL agent Leigh Steinberg says Aaron Rodgers’ public rupture with the Pittsburgh Steelers and his allegations against coach Mike McCarthy could prompt questions from agents advising potential players about joining the Steelers in the future, and tarnish Rodgers' lasting memory in the NFL.

"This is about as far away from an ideal parting as can be imagined," Steinberg told OutKick.

Steinberg, whose former clients include Steelers quarterbacks Ben Roethlisberger, Kordell Stewart and Neil O’Donnell, criticized Rodgers for taking the dispute public, saying the quarterback was undermining the kind of farewell most accomplished players hope to have.

"But for Rodgers to have this long, illustrious career and then go out this way is certainly not ideal because his critique of the team, whether accurate or not, is exposing dirty laundry to the world," he said.

Steinberg also suggested Rodgers understood exactly how much attention his comments would attract.

"Pat McAfee didn’t have to do much interviewing," he said. "He just, he asked a couple questions and Aaron took it from there."

"So he knew what he was doing."

STEELERS COACH MIKE MCCARTHY INJURES HIMSELF AND IT WAS SERIOUS ENOUGH HE NEVER GOT TO HALFTIME LOCKER ROOM

Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring during meetings and missing team events during a Wednesday appearance on ESPN’s "The Pat McAfee Show." The interview followed Pittsburgh’s announcement that Rodgers would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, with Mason Rudolph starting. NFL Network subsequently reported that Pittsburgh was waiving Rodgers.

But Steinberg said the public nature of Rodgers’ accusations did not absolve Pittsburgh of examining them.

"The Steelers have to look at themselves and ask, are any of these allegations true?" he said. "Is there dysfunction in the coaching ranks?"

Steinberg stressed that he could not independently determine whether Rodgers’ account was accurate.

"Only the people involved know," he said.

The consequences could extend beyond Rodgers’ departure, according to Steinberg, who said the allegations would warrant questions from agents helping players evaluate Pittsburgh as a destination.

Asked how he would advise a high-value client considering signing with the Steelers, he said he would seek answers directly from team leadership.

"You would certainly have discussions with their front office as to whether or not these allegations are true," he said.

Steinberg said Rodgers had described a distant, uninvolved coach, making it necessary for agents to establish the facts rather than simply accept either the quarterback’s account or the franchise’s reputation.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION JOE THEISMANN REVEALS KEY FACTOR IN AARON RODGERS DECISION TO RETURN TO STEELERS

That would mean weighing the allegations against Pittsburgh’s history of stability, including its limited coaching turnover.

"So you certainly want to understand the facts," he said.

Steinberg’s own experience with the organization offered a favorable view of its leadership. Over years of representing Pittsburgh quarterbacks, he said, the front office consistently emphasized players’ interests and the franchise’s future.

"Every discussion I ever had with their front office, they were looking to the long view. They cared about players," he said.

He also praised owner Art Rooney II and general manager Omar Khan.

"I’ve dealt many times with Omar Khan and many times with Art Rooney, and they’ve been nothing but classy."

That history, Steinberg suggested, makes the current controversy particularly difficult for an organization that has long prided itself on its culture.

"They’ve always had a reputation as the epitome of stability, class, a unique culture," he said. "When people put on the Steelers uniform, they tend to play better."

Steinberg described the deterioration of Rodgers’ relationship with McCarthy, who previously coached him in Green Bay, as "stunning."

For Steinberg, the issue was not simply that a quarterback and coach disagreed. It was that a dispute ordinarily handled inside a franchise had become a public spectacle.

He said teams generally want to work through internal criticism while presenting unity to the outside world.

Asked whether McCarthy should be held responsible for the situation, Steinberg declined to assign blame solely to the coach.

"I don’t have the inside information," he said, adding that the stories Rodgers told were "disturbing stories for a franchise."

"I’m sure they’ll take a look at the conduct and evaluate it."

His broader assessment placed responsibility on the fractured relationship.

"I think it’s a mutual breakdown," he said.

Asked whether he had seen a comparable situation involving such a high-profile player publicly criticizing his coach, Steinberg answered, "No."

"First of all, it’s shocking that Aaron Rodgers gets benched. Then it’s even more shocking that he goes public and tells the world that the coach is just not effective," he said.

Steinberg contrasted the episode with the more appreciative farewell he said players typically want, pointing to Tom Brady, Troy Aikman and Peyton Manning as examples.

Still, he expressed sympathy for Rodgers’ frustration.

"Aaron Rodgers is a proud player. He obviously has had a storied career. This was not the way he wanted to go out, so I can understand his unhappiness."

Steinberg was skeptical that another team would pick up Rodgers before the season ends, pointing to the practical challenges of joining a new organization without an offseason or training camp together.

"The difficult thing with that is he would not have had training camp with that team," he said.

Even for an accomplished quarterback, Steinberg suggested, a late-season move leaves little time to prepare and develop familiarity with a new team.

"Does a team pick him up this late in the season? Probably not," he said.

But asked whether he would drop Rodgers as a client if the quarterback wanted to continue playing, Steinberg answered: "No."

"There’s a loyalty factor there," he said.

He was more optimistic about Rodgers’ opportunities after his playing career, suggesting broadcasting, coaching or potentially team ownership as possibilities.

"I think at a certain level this will blow over. And Rodgers will be remembered for the best facets of things," Steinberg said.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

He said Rodgers could be an intriguing broadcaster because of his insights and opinions, while noting that coaching can be a difficult transition for former players.

"He’s forgotten more about football than most people will ever know," Steinberg said.

Still, he cautioned against reaching a final judgment based on the quarterback’s account alone.

"We don’t know what the reaction will be to this, because we’ve only heard one side of the story," he said.

"We haven’t heard from the Steelers."

item.title: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor dies at 65; bandmates pay emotional tribute
item.description: Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor, whose playing powered 1980s hit "Rio" and "Hungry Like the Wolf," has died at age 65 of prostate cancer, his family said.
item.content:encoded:
Duran Duran guitarist Andy Taylor has died of prostate cancer at the age of 65, Fox News Digital confirmed.

Taylor died peacefully at home surrounded by family on Monday, according to a joint statement from his family and former bandmates.

"To the world, Andy was a brilliant guitarist, but to us, he was the most wonderful husband, a loving dad and the proudest grandfather," his wife, Tracey, said on behalf of the family. 

"He was the rock of our family. For all the incredible experiences music brought him, family always came first. Nothing made him happier than having us all together, and no matter how far music took him, his heart was always at home."

DURAN DURAN GUITARIST ANDY TAYLOR IS ‘RADIOACTIVE’ AFTER ‘NUCLEAR’ CANCER TREATMENTS

His family added that the musician "faced the last few years with so much courage and determination," noting "he never gave up" and kept "fighting until the very end, never losing his love of life."

"The kindness and support shown to him by fans from all over the world throughout his illness brought him immense comfort and strength, and for that we will always be grateful," they added. "Andy knew just how deeply he was loved, and we take great comfort in that. We will miss him every single day."

Members of the band each wrote their own tribute to Taylor on the band's website, with lead singer Simon Le Bon writing, "There’s a massive Andy Taylor shaped hole in my heart."

He added that when he thinks of Taylor he remembers "the blond bombshell, firebrand teenager I met in 1980" who had "spikey hair and a spiky personality" and was an extremely talented guitar player. 

"I have so many wonderful, hilarious, tragic memories of our time together: on tour, in the studio, in our little flat on Caroline Road, Balsall Heath at 6am," he added. "And through it, & above it all he was in love with his family - most important thing in his life."

John Taylor said, "What he brought down to Birmingham on that train from Whitley Bay can never be quantified," while Nick Rhodes wrote him a poem, in which he called him "An adventurer who found his new home." 

"The 'Geordie Genius', 'the live wire from Newcastle': how fortunate we were to have found him," Roger Taylor said. 

"The incredible, talented musician and gifted songsmith arrived on a train from Cullercoats to knock us into shape and help us grow into the burgeoning version of Duran Duran that took on the world within a year or two of his arrival. 

"The sadness cuts extremely deep, but admiration and respect run even deeper for the Taylor that wasn't related but will forever be my brother. Rest in peace now, Andy."

HOLLYWOOD STARS WHO DIED IN 2026: PHOTOS

Duran Duran formed in the late 1970s, releasing their self-titled debut album in 1981 and quickly making a name for themselves as a group ready to push boundaries. They became household names with the release of their second album, "Rio," in 1982, which featured hits like "Hungry Like the Wolf."

Despite their success, the band went on hiatus in the mid-1980s, with two members, including Taylor, pursuing solo projects. He reunited with the band in 2001 but left again in 2006. As a band, they have won two Grammy Awards, have a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame and were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022.

Andy Taylor released his first solo project in over 33 years in 2023 with the album "Man's a Wolf to Man." Also in 2023, he reunited with Duran Duran one more time to play guitar on their album, "Danse Macabre."

"Andy was there at the very beginning of our story. From the moment he arrived in Birmingham from the North East with a guitar and an unshakeable belief in what we could become, he brought an indelible fire and swagger to our music," the band said in a statement. 

"His playing drove the songs that took us around the world, and with a dry wit that was matched only by his wonderfully unsentimental, no-nonsense outlook on life he kept us grounded and gave the band its edge through the extraordinary years that followed.

When we were inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2022, Andy was too unwell to join us, but his words that night reminded everyone of his strength and the bond we shared. Andy faced his illness with remarkable courage, honesty and grace."

item.title: Pat Freiermuth sidesteps Aaron Rodgers' claims about Mike McCarthy and Steelers coaching staff
item.description: Aaron Rodgers claimed Mike McCarthy dozes off in meetings, leaving Steelers tight end Pat Freiermuth dodging questions as Pittsburgh braces for Denver.
item.content:encoded:
If the Pittsburgh Steelers thought they'd get a relaxing Wednesday before Thanksgiving, they were mistaken.

Because now-former signal caller Aaron Rodgers went scorched earth on Steelers coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show," even claiming that the coach has been known to doze off in meetings.

Now, players like tight end Pat Freiermuth found themselves in front of microphones just minutes after Rodgers' bombshell interview and in a brutal spot.

AARON RODGERS NOT RETURNING TO STEELERS, SAYS MIKE MCCARTHY FALLS ASLEEP IN MEETINGS AND IS 'UNWELL'

"Yeah, listen: anything I say about the situation is going to be tough, and obviously (the situation) is tough," Freiermuth said. "Y'know, I'm here, and we're just focused on trying to get a win against Denver."

The former Penn State Nittany Lion was then asked if he had confidence in the Steelers coaching staff and the team's current direction.

WHAT’S YOUR TAKE: WILL AARON RODGERS PLAY ANOTHER SNAP THIS SEASON?

"I'm confident," he said.

Freiermuth was especially in a bind, as Rodgers claimed that the tight end was the one who broke the news that he was being benched in the first place. He was asked about the conversation he had with Rodgers over the phone.

"I was just checking in on a close friend, from what I heard," Freiermuth said. "That's all I have to say about that."

Freiermuth also steered clear of a question about whether the situation between Rodgers and the organization could've ended differently.

"Again, I'm sorry, but I'm just going to focus on Denver," he said.

It's a wise choice to put as much focus on the Broncos as possible. With the Steelers already facing a Black Friday meeting with the top team in the conference, the last thing they need is some noise creating distractions.

And, boy, is there a lot of drama here, and likely more to come.

item.title: Trump's birthright citizenship restrictions struck down again by DC federal judge he called 'hater'
item.description: Judge Christopher Cooper struck down Trump's second birthright citizenship order, citing the Fourteenth Amendment and rejecting surrogacy-based exclusions.
item.content:encoded:
A DC federal judge, previously dubbed by President Donald Trump as an "anti- Trump Hater," blocked Trump's second attempt to restrict birthright citizenship in a Wednesday ruling.

U.S. District Judge Christopher Cooper, who was recently in Trump's crosshairs after ruling against efforts to shut down the Kennedy Center for renovations and add Trump's name to the cultural institution, issued a 67-page ruling striking down an August executive order that barred U.S. -born children whose parents are suspected terrorists or gang members, or children born through surrogacy to foreign parents, from citizenship eligibility.

Cooper's ruling comes months after the Supreme Court struck down Trump's initial executive order, signed on his first day back in office. The order attempted to deny birthright citizenship to U.S.-born children whose mothers were in the country illegally or temporarily and whose fathers were neither U.S. citizens nor green card holders.

WHITE HOUSE RIPS ‘ACTIVIST’ BIDEN JUDGE WHO UPENDED TRUMP BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP ORDER

"As the Supreme Court has made clear, however, the President cannot carve out new exceptions to birthright citizenship for children born within the United States and subject to its laws," Cooper ruled.

Trump's second executive order was already partially blocked on Sept. 2 by U.S. District Judge Deborah Boardman in Maryland, whose injunction protected U.S.-born children of mothers who were in the country illegally or temporarily and whose fathers were neither U.S. citizens nor lawful permanent residents.

Cooper's ruling expanded protections beyond that class to include additional children born to certain foreign government and international organization employees, parents deemed "alien enemies" by the administration and foreign parents who used commercial surrogacy services in the U.S.

"The merits in this case are clear-cut. The Supreme Court has twice confirmed that all children born in this country are U.S. citizens, save only for the small handful who are not subject to U.S. law," Cooper wrote.

In addition to the Supreme Court's June ruling in Trump v. Barbara, Cooper referred to the high court's ruling in United States v. Wong Kim Ark, which determined that a man born to Chinese immigrants was a protected U.S. citizen under the 14th Amendment.

SEN ERIC SCHMITT SEEKS TO END BIRTH TOURISM, REVOKE CITIZENSHIP FOR BABIES OF FOREIGN DIPLOMATS

Cooper noted that Wong Kim Ark established narrow exceptions to birthright citizenship, including for children of foreign diplomats, children born aboard foreign public ships and children of enemy forces occupying American territory.

"While the Fourteenth Amendment may theoretically permit new exceptions beyond those listed in Wong Kim Ark, Congress has not authorized any such exceptions," Cooper wrote.

Cooper argued that membership in a terrorist organization alone does not satisfy the historical exception to birthright citizenship for children of enemy forces occupying U.S. territory. He criticized the Trump administration's contention that foreign invaders could occupy American territory without actually holding it as an "outside-the-box understanding" of what constitutes an occupation.

"To recap, a parent’s purported status as an alien enemy, standing alone, cannot strip a U.S.-born child of his right to birthright citizenship," Cooper wrote. "The alien-enemy exception, properly understood, applies only to children born to hostile enemy forces in temporarily occupied U.S. territory."

Cooper also rejected Trump's attempt to deny birthright citizenship to children born through commercial surrogacy arrangements involving foreign parents, finding that the circumstances of their birth do not exempt them from U.S. jurisdiction.

"Indeed, foreign parents choose surrogacy arrangements in the United States precisely to have the child be governed by U.S. law and have the surrogacy process ‘supervised by a court.," Cooper wrote.

TRUMP TO ASK SUPREME COURT TO REHEAR BIRTHRIGHT CITIZENSHIP CASE AFTER 'INSANE DECISION'

He noted that, prior to Trump's second executive order, the State Department recognized the citizenship of children born on American soil regardless of whether they were born through surrogacy.

The Trump administration is expected to appeal the decision and request that the executive order be temporarily enforced while the litigation works its way through the courts, a process that could take months.

"This is just another ruling from an activist judge appointed by Obama attempting to thwart President Trump’s commonsense agenda," White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said in a statement to Fox News Digital. "The birthright citizenship executive order is consistent with the holdings and analysis set forth by the Supreme Court."

The Justice Department could seek temporary relief from the U.S. Court of Appeals for the DC Circuit or seek intervention from the Supreme Court. Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for comment.

OBAMA-APPOINTED JUDGE WITH TIES TO ANTI-TRUMP CONSPIRACY THEORY HIT WITH MISCONDUCT COMPLAINT

In addition to ruling against Trump's Kennedy Center renovation efforts, Cooper ruled that Trump's Department of Government Efficiency must turn over records requested in a Freedom of Information Act lawsuit.

Trump has called Cooper one of the "Radical Left Democrats."

Cooper is also married to Amy Jeffress, who was Biden’s personal lawyer in 2025 and previously did some work for the Jan. 6 committee.
